And in the first year of Koresh, the king of Paras This book is arranged as a continuation of the Book of Daniel, as is explained in Baba Bathra (15a), and the word [וּבְשְׁנַת] refers back from this [book] to that one, for it is stated in Daniel (9:2): “In the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, contemplated the calculations of the number of the years that the word of Hashem had come to Yirmiyahu the prophet from the destruction of Yerushalayim, seventy years.” And so the entire chapter proceeds to relate [the story] of the destruction of the Temple, the time of the Babylonian exile, and his confession, in which he confessed Yisrael’s sin. The beginning of this book is as follows: After Belshatzar was assassinated, Daryavesh the Madai reigned, as it says (Dan. 6:1): “And Daryavesh the Madai received the kingdom etc.” and after Daryavesh’s death, this Koresh, the king of Paras, reigned, and in the first year of his reign, the seventy years for the remembrance of the Babylonian exile, [counting] from the day that Yehoyakim was exiled, were completed, as it says (Jer. 29:10): “At the completion of seventy years of Bavel, I will remember you etc.” When Yisrael returned from the Babylonian exile to the land of Yisrael, in that year, in the first year of Koresh, Yisrael laid the foundation of the Temple, and the adversaries of Yehudah and Binyamin slandered them to Koresh, the king of Paras, and he commanded [them] to curtail the work, no longer to build the edifice of the Temple; and Bnei Yisrael were idle, for they did not build the Temple during the entire reign of Koresh and Achashverosh, who succeeded him, until the second year of Daryavesh, the son of Achashverosh, the king of Paras, who was Daryavesh, the son of Esther. And in the second year of his reign, they began building the Temple until the building was completed. And from the first year of Koresh until the second year of Daryavesh, the son of Achashverosh the king of Paras, in whose days the Temple was built, were eighteen years, to fulfill what was said (Dan. 9:2): “from the destruction of Yerushalayim, seventy years etc.” And now, in the second year of Daryavesh, seventy years had elapsed since the destruction of Yerushalayim; [i.e.,] the destruction of the Temple, when Tzidkiyahu was exiled. From the exile of Yehoyakim until the exile of Tzidkiyahu, when the Temple was destroyed, were eighteen years, and now in the first year of Koresh, the king of Paras, seventy years since the exile of Yehoyakim, when Yisrael was exiled to Bavel, were completed, and thereby the verse that states (Jer. 29:10): “for at the completion of seventy years of Bavel I will remember you etc.” was fulfilled. And this is the remembrance, that Yisrael returned to their soil and built the foundation of the building of the Temple, although it was not yet completed. We find that there were fifty-two years from the exile of Tzidkiyahu, when the Temple was destroyed, until the first year of Koresh, the king of Paras; and eighteen years after the first year of Koresh, which is the second year of Daryavesh, when Yisrael commenced to build the edifice, and they completed it. This is proven in Seder Olam (ch. 29), in Tractate Megillah (11b) and in this book, as I explained.

at the completion of the word of Hashem from the mouth of Yirmiyahu at the time that the word of the Holy One, blessed be He, which Yirmiyahu spoke, was completed, as it says (Jer. 29:10): “for at the completion of seventy years of Bavel etc.”
Hashem aroused the spirit the will.
a proclamation He proclaimed a proclamation throughout his kingdom.
and also in writing And he also sent his letter throughout his kingdom about this matter.
saying And so he said to them in his proclamation that he proclaimed and in his epistle that he sent throughout his kingdom.
So said Koresh, the king of Paras...delivered to me that I am the king and ruler over all the kingdoms.

and He commanded me He commanded me through Yeshayahu the prophet to build for Him the Temple in Yerushalayim, as it says in the Book of Yeshayahu (44:28): “Who says to Koresh, ‘He is My shepherd, and all My desire he shall fulfill,’ and to say to Yerushalayim, ‘It shall be built, and the Temple shall be founded.’” (ibid. 45:1): “So said Hashem to His anointed one, to Koresh, whose right hand I held....” And this prophecy was already stated by lsaiah.
in Yerushalayim, which is in Yehudah whch is in the province of Yehudah.

Who is among you So did he announce and write to all the kingdoms, “Who is among you of all His people,” [i.e., of the people] of the Holy One, blessed be He, may the Holy One, blessed be He, be at his assistance, and let him ascend to build His house that is in Yerushalayim.
And whoever remains and every Yehudi who remains in his place, who cannot ascend because he has no money.

shall help him I command the people of his place to provide him and help him with silver, gold, possessions and cattle, in order that he be able to ascend to Yerushalayim with the donation that the people of his place will donate for the building of the Temple, for also among the nations there were some who contributed donations to the building of the Temple.
to the House of Elokim, which is in Yerushalayim From “So said Koresh” until here is the proclamation and the message of the written epistle.
of Yehudah and Binyamin the heads of the families of the tribes of Yehudah and Binyamin.
all whom... inspired They ascended to Yerushalayim to build the Temple with all those whom Hashem inspired to ascend and to build the Temple.

And all those around them And all the nations who were Yisrael’s neighbors assisted and strengthened the hands of the Yehudim with gold and silver and all these gifts in order that they be able to ascend to Yerushalayim.
besides all that was donated All this the neighbors of the Yehudim did, besides what they [the Yehudim] themselves donated for the building of the Temple.
and had placed them in the temple of his god that Nevuchadnetzar had placed in the temple of his pagan deity.
by the hand of Mithderath the treasurer such was the name of Koresh’s treasurer, and Koresh commanded [him] to take them out.

and he counted them out This treasurer counted them and delivered them to Sheshbatzar, so that he would carry them and transport them to Yerushalayim. Our Rabbis said: “Sheshbatzar is identical with Daniel, and why was he called Sheshbatzar? Because he endured six troubles (שֵּׁשּׁ צָרוֹת) .”
the prince of Yehudah He is the prince of the tribe of Yehudah.
their number of the vessels of the House of Hashem.
basins Heb. אֲגַרְטְלֵי. They are kinds of vessels.

knives Heb. מַחֲלָפִים. They are knives, and this expression refers to the chamber of the knives (בֵּית הַחֲלִיפוֹת). Because they would deposit the knives therein, it was called the chamber of the depository of the knives (לִשְּׁכַּת בֵּית הַחֲלִיפוֹת).

bowls Heb. כְּפוֹרֵי, bowls, and they were called כְּפוֹרֵי from an expression of wiping, like (Bava Mezia 24b): “who wiped (דְּכָפַר) his hands on his neighbor’s cloak,” because the one who would receive the blood in a bowl would wipe the squirtings of the blood that splattered on his hand on the rim of the bowl.
secondary Heb. מִשְּׁנִים, secondary ones, other vessels of another kind.
All the vessels Now he totals the sum of those counted and those who were not counted all into one number, but the important ones he counts.
when the exiles were brought up Heb. הֵעָלוֹת, [a passive] expression.

And these are the people of the province These are the Children of Yisrael who are from the province of the land of Yisrael, who are now coming up to Yerushalayim from the captivity that is in the exile.
and they returned And now they returned to Yerushalayim.
and Yehudah And the people of Yehudah returned, each one to his city.
[Those] who came these people of the province, in the beginning, when they went into exile from Yisrael to Bavel with Zerubavel etc.

Mispar...the number Heb. מִסְפָּר. [This word appears twice in this verse.] In the first one, the “pay” is vowelized with a “kamatz,” and it is the name of a man; in the second, the “pay” is vowelized with a “pattah”, and it is the construct state, [meaning the number of].
the important men of the people of Yisrael These were the great and important people, and the others followed them. Therefore, they were counted after them separately.

The children of Parosh, etc. There are some in the chapter for whom the father’s name is used for the family name [surname] and there are some who are called by the name of their place, i.e., “the children of such-and-such a place.”

The priests: the children of Yedayah Until here, he counted the children of Yehudah and Binyamin, and from now on he counts the priests and the Leviyim, as he says above (1:5): “So the heads of the families of Yehudah and Binyamin and the priests and the Leviyim arose....”
The singers The Leviyim who were singers, and likewise, the gatekeepers are Leviyim who were gatekeepers of the gates of the Temple.
The Nethinim Now he counts those Nethinim who were woodcutters and water-drawers for the congregation, and from there they derived their livelihood.
and the children of Shlomo’s slaves King Shlomo had slaves, and these children were of their descendants.
And these were the ones who ascended from Tel-Mela, etc. And what incident happened to them? They could not tell....
and their children [i.e., the children] of their fathers, because they lost their genealogical records and did not know if they were Bnei Yisrael.
The children of Dlayah They too are included in “these were the ones who ascended from Tel- Melah.”
who took Each one of the sons of Barzilai the Giladi took a wife.
and was called by their name And the name of Barzilai was called on their name because they took of his daughters.
These referring to the priests, who had to trace their lineage with that record, and who could not find the record of their lineage.

and they were disqualified Heb. וַיְגאַלוּ, for they were defiled and purged from the priesthood that they should no longer perform the service with the remaining priests, because their genealogical record was not found.

Hattirshatha That is Nechemyah, the son of Hachaliah (Neh. 8:9), and our Rabbis said (Yerushalmi Kid. 4:1) that he was named Hattirshatha because the Sages permitted him (הָתֵּר) to drink (שָּׁתָּא) wine of gentiles because he was the king’s butler.
of the most holy sacrifices sin-offerings and guilt-offerings, like the other priests.

until a priest arises, etc. like a person who says to his friend, “Until the Messiah comes, this matter will not come about.” I cannot interpret it to mean: until a priest arises for the Urim and Tumim in the Second Temple, because we find in Yoma, chapter 1 (21b) that the Urim and Tumim were missing in the Second Temple.

The entire congregation together When they were all together with the priests, the Leviyim and the Nethinim, they amounted to this number; and the Children of Yisrael counted above were of the tribe of Yehudah and Binyamin, and those missing from this number, which you will not find above, were of the other tribes. So it is explained in Seder Olam (ch. 29): “‘The entire congregation together was forty-two thousand etc.’ But if you add them up, they are only thirty thousand. Where are the thirteen thousand? They ascended from the other tribes.”
Besides their slaves and their bondwomen who were not included in the congregation.

and they had two hundred male and female singers because they were going up joyfully from Bavel to the land of Yisrael, they required male and female singers in order that they should stroll among them in their great joy.
donated They were donating toward the building of the Temple.
According to their ability according to their ability and their money.
drachmas Heb. דַּרְכְּמוֹנִים, the name of a golden coin.
and priests’ tunics in which to serve.
arrived Heb. וַיִגַע like וְהִגִיעַ, it reached.
The seventh month That is the month of Tishrei, and the Children of Yisrael who were in the cities, what did they do? They all gathered as one to Yerushalayim.

And they set the altar on its bases in order to offer up sacrifices upon it, because they were afraid of the peoples of the land, lest they taunt them and lest they slander them to the king. And they built the altar to offer up burnt offerings upon it, in order that the peoples hear and understand the matter, that they did it with the sanction of the king and therefore they would hesitate to taunt them about the building of the Temple.
for the morning and for the evening the daily sacrifice of the morning and the daily sacrifice of twilight.
and the burnt offering of each day in its day, in the number the sacrifices of the Festivals in their number, according to their ordinance.
And afterwards And after Sukkot they would offer up sacrifices every day, for the morning and for the evening.
and for the New Moon lit. and for the months. And at the beginning of the months they would offer up the sacrifices of the New Moon.
and for all the appointed seasons of Hashem and for the rest of the appointed seasons of their sacrifices.

and for everyone who willingly offered And for all those who willingly offered their free-will offerings, the priests would accept them to sacrifice them, and from the first day of Tishrei they commenced to offer up sacrifices, but the foundation of the Temple was not yet built.
to the Zidonians and to the Tzorim the people of Tzor and Zidon, who were the artisans who built the Temple.
to the sea of Jaffa By way of the sea they would bring them.

according to the sanction of Heb. כְּרִשְׁיוֹן as the sanction of the king was upon them to build the Temple. כְּרִשְׁיוֹן is an expression of permission (רְשּׁוּת) derived from רשּׁה ; since from אבה to want, he says [i.e., derives] אֶבְיוֹן, a needy person; and from צבה, to desire, צִבְיוֹן, desire; and from חזה to see, חִזָיוֹן, a vision; and from רעה, רַעְיוֹן, thought; from חבה, חֶבְיוֹן, hiding; and from רשּׁה, he says רְשּׁוּת, permission; like from, ענה, עֱנוּת, affliction; and from שּׁבה, שְּׁבוּת,captivity; and from ראה, רְאוּת, a sight; and from זנה, זְנוּת, harlotry. The result is that רְשּׁוּת and רִשְׁיוֹן are derived from the same root according to the gauge of grammar, and they are the same expression. Menachem, (p. 34) however, associated it with (Ps. 21:3): “and the speech of his lips (וַַַַַאֲרֶשֶּׁת),” but he was not exact with its root. Nevertheless, these two manners [of defining words] are close to each other in their meanings.
in the second month That is the month of Iyar.
from the captivity all those who came from the captivity to Yerushalayim.
and they stationed They stationed the Levi singers to harmonize and to recite a song before the builders at the time of the building of the foundation of the Temple.
to conduct Heb. לְנַצֵחַ. These two expressions of נִצוּחַ are harmonies of song, like (Ps. 4:1): “To the conductor (לַּמְנַצֵחַ), a song of David.”
And Yeshua...stood They stood and recited the song together around the ones who did the work of the foundation of the Temple.

And...laid the foundation וְיִסְדוּ This is the strong conjugation of יְסוֹד, like (Ezek. 25:4): “and they will settle (וְיִשְּׁבוּ) their palaces.” Just as וְיִשְּׁבוּ is derived from ישּׁב so is וְיִסְדוּ derived from יסד, and their meaning is, וְיִסְדוּ וְיִשְּׁבוּ in the intensive conjugation with two “yud”s, one for the [continuous] action and one for the radical, and their meaning is that they were laying the foundation, they were settling.

And the builders laid the foundation And the builders were laying the foundation [see above] of the Temple of Hashem at the time [that] they were harmonizing in their song, and they stationed the priests attired with elegant garments with trumpets in their hands to sound them.
and the Leviyim the sons of Asaf were the singers.
with cymbals Heb. בַּמְצִלְתַּיִם, like (Ps. 150:9): “with loud sounding cymbals (בְּצִלְצְלֵי שָּׁמַע).” They are musical instruments.
through David for they were harmonizing and singing songs of David, the king of Yisrael.
And they sang aloud Heb. וַיַעֲנוּ, an expression of raising the voice in song, like (Exod. 15: 21): “And Miriam raised her voice in song to them.”
and with thanks and with thanksgivings.
for it is good to give thanks to Hashem.
and the entire people the rest of the people of Yisrael.
because...was laid They acted with all these rejoicings because of the building of the foundation, which was laid in the House of Hashem.
when its foundation was laid Heb. בְּיָסְדוֹ, with its foundation. With the noun of יוֹסֶד and from יסד, he says בְּיָסְדוֹ, like from חדֶשּׁ, בְּחָדְשּׁוֹ, and from קדֶשּׁ, בְּקָדְשּׁוֹ.
this Temple When they would see the building of this Temple, they would weep because they remembered the large building of the First Temple.
and many who had not seen the building of the First Temple, were rejoicing and shouting for joy with a loud voice, out of their great joy that they had emerged from their exile.

And the people did not recognize Those listeners did not recognize the voice of the shout of joy, because of the voice of the people’s weeping, for the rejoicing people were shouting with a great shout, and the voice of weeping was heard farther and farther away.

the adversaries of Yehudah and Binyamin They are the nations whom Sannecherib settled in the land Yisrael, as it says (II Kings 17:24): “And the king of Ashur brought [people] from Bavel and from Kutah and from Avvah and from Chamat and from Sfarvayim, and he settled them in the cities of Shomron instead of the Children of Yisrael.”
and said to them, “Let us build with you...” They said this in order that through them the work of the Temple should be disrupted, that they should build no more.

since the days of Esarchadon the king of Ashur the son of Sannecherib, for after Sannecherib settled them there, as it says (II Kings 19:37, Isa. 37:38): “And he was prostrating himself in the temple of Nisroch his god, and Adramelech and Sharezer, his sons, slew him by the sword etc., and his son Esarchadon reigned in his stead.”
but we Heb. כִּי, but we alone shall build. This כִּי serves in place of אֶלָּא, but.
the people of the land They are the adversaries of Yehudah and Binyamin.
were hindering to disrupt them from their work.
from building Heb. לִבְנוֹת, lit. to build, and so (Gen. 41:49): “until one ceased to count (לִסְפֹּר).”
And they would hire Heb. וְסֹכְרִים. This is written with a “sammech,” but its meaning is as though it was written with a “sin,” [meaning] that they would hire advisors to disrupt the work.
all the days of the reign of Koresh and the reign of Achashverosh, who reigned after Koresh, until the second year of Daryavesh, who reigned after Achashverosh, the work was stopped.
And in the reign of Achashverosh who reigned after Koresh; he is the Achashverosh who took Esther.
they wrote an accusation not to build the Temple.
against the dwellers of Yehudah and Yerushalayim to inform on them and to chide them not to build the Temple.

And in the days of Artachshasta He is Koresh, the king of Paras. The numerical value of the letters of כּרֶשּׁ equal the numerical value of the letters of דָּרְיָוֶשּׁ: [כ = 20; ר = 200; שּׁ = 300; total = 520. ד = 4; ר = 200; י = 10; 520 ו = 6; שּׁ = 300; total = 520.] And so we learned in Tractate Rosh Hashanah (3b): “The same one is Koresh, who is Daryavesh, who is Artachshasta.” [He was called Koresh כּרֶשּׁ because he was a worthy (כָּשֵּׁר) king; Artachshasta, because of the kingdom, and in Seder Olam (ch. 30): “Daryavesh was Artachshasta (אַרְתַּחְשַּׁשְּׁתָּא), and the entire kingdom was called Artachshasta, etc.” [meaning that all the kings were called Artachshasta].
wrote with peace wrote his letter with words of peace.
Mitredat Tave'el This is the name of a man, one of the adversaries of Yehudah and Binyamin.
and the rest of his colleagues Heb. כְּנָותָיו, his companies and his societies.
to Artachshasta [as translated,] to Artachshasta.
and the script of the epistle Heb. וּכְתָב הַנִשְּׁתְּוָן.
written in Aramaic in Aramaic characters.
and explained in Aramaic The script was explained in the Aramaic language.
Rechum was the secretary Rechum was the secretary and the master of words to compose the epistle.

and Shimshai was the scribe And Shimshai was the scribe: he is Shimshai the son of Haman. So it is customary to mention the scribe and the secretary together because they need each other; one composes and dictates, and the scribe writes, as it says (I Kings 4:3): “Eliphoreph and Achiyah, the sons of Shisha, scribes, Yehoshafat, the son of Ahlud, the secretary,” and in another place it says (Isa. 36: 22): “And Elyakim, the son of Chilkiyahu etc. and Shevna the scribe, and Yoach, the son of Asaf the secretary, came.”
they wrote a letter These two, Rechum and Shimshai, wrote the letter as Mitredat Tave'el had commanded them, and they all were dwellers of the cities of Shomron.
about Yerushalayim about the building of the Temple, which is in Yerushalayim.
as is stated Aram. כְּנֵמָא, as is stated, and that is similar to the expression of the Gemara: “as we wish to say further.”
Then Aram. אֱדַיִן, equivalent to the Hebrew אָז.
Rechum the name of a man.
the secretary Aram. בְּעֵל טְעֵם secretary and master of words.
the Dinites, the Apharesattechites, etc. All these are names of nations whom Sancheriv repatriated in the cities of Shomron.
the Apharesites They are the Paras whom Sancheriv settled in the cities of Shomron.
the Archevites They are the people of Arkovaye, as it says (Gen. 10:10): “and Arkovaye and Akad and Kalne.”
the Babylonians the people of Bavel.
the Shushanchites the people of Shushan, the capital.
the Elamites the people of Eilam. Sancheriv settled all of these peoples in the land of Yisrael, and all of them were settling and concurring with the commission of this letter.
And the rest of the nations and the rest of the nations that Sancheriv exiled; they have all concurred.
Asenappar Sancheriv.
the great and honored for he was a great and honored king, as it says (Isa. 36:4): “So has the great king, the king of Ashur, said.”
in the cities of Shomron in the cities surrounding Shomron.

and the rest of the other side of the river and the rest of the nations that are on the other side of the river; because the river Perat intervenes between the land of Yisrael and Bavel, those nations that are in Yisrael are on the opposite side of the river of those found in Bavel.
and Ke’eneth a name of a place; and all the people of Ke’eneth have concurred with the commission of this letter.
This is the meaning of the letter and this is the interpretation of the letter.
the meaning Aram. פַּרְשֶּׁגֶן like (Esther 3:14): “The meaning of (פַּתְשֶּׁגֶן) the writ.
that they sent to him [as translated,] that they sent to him.
to Artachshasta [as translated,] to Artachshasta.

Your servants are the people of the other side of the river and Ke’eneth The people of the other side of the river and the people of Ke’eneth are your servants. All the nations counted here are included in this generalization, for they were all on the side of the land of Yisrael, which is on the opposite side of the river of those dwelling in Bavel, and this is the beginning of the letter: “Your servants are the people of the other side of the river etc.” until, “...you will have no part.”
Let it be known to the king Let it be a known thing to the king.
that the Yehudim that the Yehudim who ascended from you upon us have come to Yerushalayim.
the rebellious and sinful city they are building [as translated,] a rebellious and sinful city they are building.
the walls they have completed [as translated,] the walls they have completed.
and the walls [as translated,] and the walls.
they have joined Aram. יָחִיטוּ, an expression of a thread, like (Gen. 14:23): “not from a thread, (מִחוּטּ),” for they are “sewing” and joining the walls one to another.
Now let it be known Now let it be known to the king.
that if this city is built [as translated,] that if this city is built.
this [as translated,] this.
and the walls are founded [as translated,] and the walls are founded.
the king’s due, the head tax, or the meal tax They are types of taxes and the money for the head taxes.
they will not give They will no longer pay taxes.
and the tax of the kings will suffer [as translated,] and the tax of the kings will suffer, for they will no longer give tax to the kings.

Now in view of this, that we wish to destroy the Temple Now in view of this matter, that we wish to implement the destruction of the Temple. דִי מְלַח is an expression of destruction and desolation, like Jer. 17:6): “barren (מְלֵחָה) land that is uninhabitable.”
we wish to destroy We wish to demolish and to destroy.
and... the king’s disgrace Aram. וְעַרְוַת מַלְכָּא, lit. and the king’s nakedness.
it is improper Aram. לָא אַרִיךְ, it is improper for us to see. אַרִיךְ means proper, like “Is it proper (אַרִיךְ) or improper (לָא אַרִיךְ)?” in Tractate Succah (44b).
therefore therefore we have sent and notified the king.
That one should search that a seeker should search and seek in the annals of your fathers, the first kings.
and you will find And you will find in the annals, and you will know that this city is a rebellious city, and it injures the kings and the countries.
and they have made rebellion in its midst And its inhabitants were making rebellion in its midst, for Yisrael would rebel against the kings of the nations.
since days of yore Aram. מִן יוֹמָת עָלְמָא, from days of yore. Since ancient times, it has been their custom to rebel against the kings of the nations.
because of this Because of this, this city was destroyed.
We make known to the king [as translated,] we make known to the king.
that if this city that if this city is built, and its walls are founded.
because of this In view of this and because of this, you will have no part in the entire other side of the river, because Yisrael will rebel against you and take everything out of your hands.
in the other side of the river That is the entire area of the side of Yisrael, which is on the other side of the river of those who are in Bavel.
The king sent a word Aram. פִּתְגָּמָא שְּׁלַח מַלְכָּא

to Rechum the secretary to Rechum the secretary, and Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their companies, who dwelt in the cities of Shomron, and to the rest of the nations who were on the other side of the river of the side of the land of Yisrael.
Shelam and Ke’eth They are places, like “and Ke’eneth.” Sometimes he calls it this and sometimes that.
The letter The writ of the letter that you sent to us was explained and read before me.
the order was given And the order was given by me, the matter of a command that I commanded.
and they searched and found And they searched in the annals of the kings and found written that this city, from days of yore, would raise itself up and exalt itself over all the kings of the nations.
and rebellion. and disobedience were committed there to rebel against the kings of the nations.

And mighty kings and mighty kings were in Yerushalayim who were the rulers and governors over the entire side of the river on the side of Yisrael, as it says regarding Shlomo (I Kings 5:4): “For he had dominion over all this side of the river, etc.” And taxes and the head tax were given to them, for the nations paid them tribute.

Now issue an order Now give out a word to announce in the land to stop these men, the Children of Yisrael, from the work, and the city of Yerushalayim shall not be built until orders are given with my knowledge and my authorization.
And beware of committing an error And you shall beware of committing any postponement or error. שָּׁלוּ is desto(u)rber in Old French, to violate.
of committing...in this matter [as translated,] of committing in this manner.
Why should...increase Why should the act of destruction in this city increase to injure the kings? Until here is Koresh’s reply, which he sent back.
then [as translated,] then.
since the interpretation Since the interpretation of the writ of the letter of Artachshasta the king—he is Koresh—this incident took place.

was read before for the writ of this letter was read before Rechum and Shimshai and their companies, and they went with speed and haste to Yerushalayim, to the Yehudim, and stopped them with force and might from continuing the construction of the edifice.
to the Yehudim Aram. עַל יְהוּדָיֵא, lit. On the Yehudim.
and they Aram. הִמוֹ, equivalent to הֵם.

Then Then the work of the building of the House of Elokim, which was in Yerushalayim, was suspended until the second year of Daryavesh, the king of Paras; for after Koresh, Achashverosh, who married Esther, reigned, and after Achashverosh, Daryavesh, the son of Achashverosh, who was the son of Esther, reigned. And from the first year of Koresh, the king of Paras, until the second year of Daryavesh were eighteen years, which completed the seventy years from the destruction of Yerushalayim. For from the destruction of the Temple, when Tzidkiyahu was exiled, until the first year of Koresh, were fifty-two years, as is explained in Seder Olam (ch. 29). There were then eighteen years from the first year of Koresh until the second year of Daryavesh, totaling a complete seventy years, and in the second year of Daryavesh they commenced to build the Temple until they completed it.

Now Chaggai the prophet...prophesied And now in the second year of Daryavesh, there came a prophecy to Chaggai and Zecharyah, the prophets to the Yehudim who were in the land of Yehudah and in Yerushalayim, in the Name of the Elokim of Yisrael to them, to build the edifice of the Temple without the authorization of King Daryavesh.
to the Yehudim Aram. עָל יְהוּדָיֵא lit. On the Yehudim.
to them Aram. עֲלֵיהוֹן, lit. on them.
Then [as translated,] then.
and commenced They began to build the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is in Yerushalayim, and with them were the prophets of the Holy One, blessed be He, helping and assisting them.
At that time, there came upon them At that time, there came upon them these adversaries of Yehudah and Binyamin to accuse and to slander them regarding the matter of the building.
the governor of the other side of the river [as translated,] the governor of the other side of the river.
and their companies [as translated,] and their companies.
and so they said to them [as translated,] and so they said to them.
Who issued to you Who ordered you, regarding the matter of building the Temple?

and to found these walls Aram. וְאֻשַּׁרְנָא, and to found these walls, like (4:12): “and the walls (וְאֻשַּׁיָא) they have joined,” the building of walls of bricks (לְבֵנִים) so did Menachem (p. 36) associate it.
Then [as translated,] then.
as we will say [as translated,] as we will say.
they said to them Those adversaries of Yehudah and Binyamin said to them [i.e.,] to Yisrael.
What are What are the names of the men?
who...this who are building this building.
And the eye of their Elokim And the eye of the Holy One, blessed be He, Who is their Elokim, was on the elders of the Yehudim to upraise them (sic) in the work of the building.
and they did not stop them And they did not stop the builders.
until the matter came to Daryavesh And the elders of the Yehudim answered a word to those adversaries that they should not stop the building until the matter would go to King Daryavesh.
and then they would answer And then the Yehudim would answer the writ of the letter concerning this, concerning Daryavesh’s reply.
The interpretation the interpretation of the text of the letter.
and his companies [as translated,] and his companies.
the Apharsechites They are one nation that was in their companies.
to King Daryavesh Aram. עַל דָּרְיָוֶשּׁ מַלְכָּא, lit. on King Daryavesh.
to him Aram. עֲלוֹהִי, lit. on him.
and so was written in it and so was written in the letter.
all peace All peace shall be his.
Let it be known to the king Let it be a known thing to the king.
that we went that we went to the land of the province of Yehudah, to the House of the great God.
and it is built And it, the House, is built.
marble Aram. גְּלָּל (marmre in Old French), marble.
and wood is laid in the walls And wood is placed in the walls to reinforce the building in order that it endure for a long time.
was done quickly Aram. אָסְפַּרְנָא מִתְעַבְדָה, was done quickly.
אָסְפַּרְנָא is (espleytosement in Old French), rapidly.
and they succeeded at it Aram. וּמַצְלַח בְּיֶדְהם. And this work was successful in their hands.
Then When we saw the building, we asked these elders.
as follows we said to them As we will say immediately following, we said to them.
Who issued to you Who issued to you the authorization to build this house and to found these walls?
and...wall the building of a wall of bricks.
also...their names We also asked them the names of the builders, the heads of the construction, in order to let you know.
that we should write that we should write to you the names of the men.
who are at their head in whose counsel and authorization they arose to build the House.
And as follows Aram. וּכְנֵמָא, as we shall state the matter.
they gave us a reply They answered us a word.
We are We are the servants of the Elokim of the heavens and the earth.
and we are building the House And we are building the House that was built many years ago.
and a great king of Yisrael And a great king that Yisrael had, viz. King Shlomo, built it and founded it.
But now But now, since our forefathers angered the Elokim of the heavens, He delivered them into the hands of the Kasdi king of Bavel, and he destroyed this House and exiled the people to Bavel.
But But in the first year of Koresh, king of Bavel, Koresh issued a command to build the House.

And also the vessels the holy vessels of silver and gold, which Nevuchadnetzar had taken out of the Temple that is in Yerushalayim and brought to his temple that is in Bavel. Koresh took them out of the temple of the king of Bavel and delivered them to the hand of Sheshbatzar—Daniel, who was called by that name.
and brought them [as translated,] and brought them.
had taken out [as translated,] had taken them out.
whom he appointed governor for he was a prince and a governor and was called by the name governor.

And he said to him And so did Koresh say to Sheshbatzar, “Take these vessels and bring them down into the Temple that is in Yerushalayim, and the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, shall be built on its place.”
then [as translated,] then.

this Sheshbatzar Aram. דֵּךְ, came and built the walls of the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, that is in Yerushalayim, and from then until now, the House has been built, but the building has not been completed.
And now And now, if it pleases the king, let the matter be known and searched out in the king’s archives, which is located in Bavel.
whether it is so whether this incident is so, that permission was issued by Koresh to build this House, which is in Yerushalayim.
and the will of the king And the will of the king concerning this he shall send to us.
to us Aram. עֲלֶינָא, lit. on us. Until here is the text of the letter that Tatnai and Shtar Bozenai sent.
Then then when the letter reached Daryavesh’s hand.
gave an order The king ordered the matter.
and they searched They searched in the library where the archives were stored in Bavel.

And there was found in a pouch And a text of one scroll was found there in an אַחְמְתָא. So did the interpreters interpret, that it is a receptacle made for letters, written sheets and books, and they established it from the root of (Gen. 21:14): “a skin of water (וְחֵמַת מַיִם),” and the “aleph” in the word is not a radical, like the rest of the Aramaic language.
in the citadel in that citadel that was in the province of Madai.
and so was written and so was written therein its memorandum.
the House of Elokim in Yerushalayim regarding the House of Elokim in Yerushalayim; what should be with it? “The House should be built.”
a place where they offer up sacrifices which is a place where they offer up sacrifices.
and its walls should be founded Aram. וְאֻשּׁוֹהִי. And its walls should be founded, like (4:12): “and its walls (וְאֻשַּׁיָא) they have joined.”
its height sixty cubits the height of the House was sixty cubits, and sixty cubits was its width.
rows Aram. נִדְבָּכִין, an expression for walls. The walls were of marble. marble Aram. גְּלָל (marmre in Old French).
and a row and a wall of new wood from within, in the manner of the building of the Temple that Shlomo built.
and the expenditures And the expenditures for the needs of the House and for the other matters pertaining to the House shall be given them from the royal palace.
And also the vessels of and also the sacred vessels of the House of Elokim, of gold and silver, which Nevuchadnetzar took out of the Temple in Yerushalayim and brought to Bavel.
let them be given over [as translated,] let them be given over.
and brought which he brought.
and brought Let all this work be brought to the Temple that is in Yerushalayim, to its place.
and it shall be deposited And it shall be deposited in the House of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Now, Tatnai This is the reply with which Daryavesh answered Tatnai and Shethar-Bozenai.
who are on the other side of the river to the side of the land of Yisrael, which is the other side of the river to those in Bavel
distance yourselves from there Distance yourselves from the building of the Temple, so that you do not disturb the workers.
this [as translated,] this.
the governors of the Yehudim The rulers of the Yehudim shall do this thing.
and to the elders of the Yehudim And to the elders of the Yehudim I command.
this House of Elokim [as translated,] this House of Elokim.
And from me shall be issued an order And from me this command will go forth.
regarding what you shall do regarding that building, the work that you shall do with these elders of the Yehudim to build the House of the Holy One, blessed be He.
and from the king’s property And from the king’s property they shall make ths building.

from the taxes of the other side of the river from the taxes of the other side of the river, which belong to the king. taxes Aram. מִדַּת, tax, like (4:13): “the king’s due (מִנְדָּה), the head tax, or the meal tax.” quickly Aram. אָסְפַּרְנָא. The building shall quickly be built; esploytosemant in Old French.
The expenses shall be given The expenses shall be given to these men so that they should not idle from their work.
And what they require and what they are concerned about.
and young bulls young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the Elokim of heaven.

wheat for fine flour. salt for sacrifices. wine for libations. and oil for the meal-offerings. When the priests who are in Yerushalayim will say [what they need], that shall be given to them the requirements of each day on its day.
without delay Aram. דִּי לָא שָּׁלוּ (son destorber in Old French).
That they should in order that they should offer up pleasing sacrificing to the Elokim of the heavens, and that they should pray for the life of the king and his children.
And an order is issued by me And a command is issued by me, along with the issue of a word regarding any person who disobeys this word.
shall be torn Aram. יִתְנְסַח. The beams of his house shall be destroyed. יִתְנְסַח is like (Deut. 28:63): “and you shall be uprooted (וְנִסַחְתֶּם) from the land.”
and a gallows upon which to place him And a gallows upon which to hang him shall be [raised up] high, so that he be hanged upon the gallows.
and his house shall be made a dungheap and his house shall be made a dungheap because of this.
נְוָלוּ connotes filth and excrement.
And Elokim, Who caused His name to rest there [as translated,] and Elokim, Who caused His name to rest there.
will cast down will cast down and destroy any such king and any such people that will stretch forth a hand to lay waste and destroy His house that is in Yerushalayim.
have issued an edict I have issued a command concerning this matter, that the building be constructed swiftly. Until here is Daryavesh’s reply.
as was said [as translated,] as was said.
acted swiftly [as translated,] acted swiftly.

And the elders of the Yehudim And the elders of the Yehudim were building and succeeding in their work, according to the prophecy of Chaggai and Zecharyah, and they built and founded the building by the command of the Elokim of Yisrael and by the authorization of Koresh, the first king of Paras, in whose days the laying of the foundation was commenced, and by the authorization of this Daryavesh, the king of Paras.
and Artachshasta He is Daryavesh, but he was called Artachshasta because of the province and the kingdom, for all kings of Paras were thus named just as all the kings of Mitzrayim were called Paroh.

And the completion of this House And the end of the completion of this House was until the third day of the month of Adar, which is the sixth year of King Daryavesh; hence the building of the House took four years.
And they offered up for the dedication They offered up for the dedication of this House these sacrifices, and it was a temporary ruling.
Now they set up the priests in their divisions for the priests were divided in their service and the Leviyim in their watches.
the Passover [offering] Now Yisrael made the Passover offering on this fourteenth of Nissan, which followed this Adar, when the building was completed.
and for themselves Heb. וְלָהֶם, lit. and for them, and for themselves.
and whoever separated They are the proselytes, who were separated from the defilement of the nations to cleave to Yisrael.

and turned the heart of the king of Ashur toward them And the Holy One, blessed be He, turned the heart of the king of Ashur toward Bnei Yisrael who were dwelling under his dominion in the land of Ashur, to strengthen them and to assist in the work of the building.
And after these incidents of the building of the House.
Artachshasta That is Daryavesh.
and the king granted him [i.e., King] Daryavesh.

according to the command of Hashem his Elokim upon him as the Holy One, blessed be He, had commanded him. This verse is transposed [its meaning being]: and the King granted him his entire request, according to the command of Hashem upon him. And our Rabbis said (Meg. 15a) that Ezra and Malachi were one and the same.
in the seventh year That is a year after the completion of the Temple.
of Artachshasta That is Daryavesh.
in the fifth month i.e., the month of Av, for the first of the month of Nissan was the beginning of their ascent from Bavel, and on the first of the month of Av they arrived in Yerushalayim.
was the commencement of the ascent the foundation of the commencement of the ascent.
according to the...hand of his Elokim as the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, caused him to succeed, for His hand was good upon him to make him succeed in his way.
For Ezra... Therefore, he went and prospered in his way, because Ezra prepared his heart, etc. He gives a reason for his words.
And this is the interpretation of the writ Heb. פַתְשֶּׁגֶן הַכְּתָב.
and His statutes to Yisrael and His statutes that He commanded Yisrael to keep.
the Book of Law [as translated,] the Book of Law.
who has mastered... and Ke’eneth He has mastered it in his hand.
An order is issued by me The authorization emanates from me that whoever of Yisrael, of the priests, or of the Leviyim, whose heart prompts him to go to Yerushalayim, may go with you.
Because of this Because of this, you are sent from the king and his seven advisors who saw the king’s face.
and his seven advisors and his seven advisors; they are the seven who see the king’s face.
to search out Yehudah An order to seek and to search out the Yehudim who are in Yerushalayim, to see whether they are engaged in the Torah of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is in your hand.
And to bring and to bring the silver and gold of the king and his advisors that they donated to the Elokim of Yisrael, to maintain His House, Whose habitation and House are in Yerushalayim.

And all the silver and gold and all the silver and gold that you will find in the province of Bavel, together with the donations of the people and the priests that they will donate to the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is in Yerushalayim; you shall take everything to Yerushalayim.

Because of this And because of this, because it is for the service of the Sanctuary, you shall quickly purchase with this money cattle, rams and lambs; sacrifices, meal-offerings, and libations, and you shall offer them up on the altar of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And what pleases you And what pleases you and your brethren (to do) with the rest of the silver and the gold, according to the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, you shall do.
And the vessels And the vessels that are given to you for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, give in their entirety before the Holy One, blessed be He, in Yerushalayim.

And the rest of the necessities and the rest of the necessities that you will require for the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, to purchase, for which you will have to give the money; you shall give from the royal treasury.

And from me—I And from me—I, King Daryavesh—is issued a command and an authorization to all the treasurers who are on the other side of the river of the side of Yisrael, who receive my taxes from the nations, that anything that Ezra the priest, the scholar of the Law of the Holy One, blessed be He, requests of you, shall be performed quickly. They should not delay his request up to a hundred talents of silver, with which to purchase sacrifices, and a hundred kors of wheat for meal-offerings, and up to a hundred measures of wine for the libations, and a hundred measures of oil to mingle the meal- offerings, and salt for the sacrifices, according to the matter that is stated (Lev. 2:13): “And every meal-offering you shall salt with salt.”
which is not written And salt, regarding which no measure is written, they shall give according to how much is needed.

Whatever is with the authorization Whatever is with the authorization of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His command, shall be done with alacrity, with the seal of the king for the House of the Holy One, blessed be He.
with a seal Aram. אַדְרַזְדָּא, seal in Arabic.
for why should there be For why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons? Therefore, the treasurers shall provide all the needs of the House.

And we are making known to you And we are making known to you that [over] all the priests, the Leviyim, the musicians, the gatekeepers, and the Nethinites, who are wood cutters and water drawers for the altar, and those who serve in this House of the Holy One, no man shall be empowered over them to levy upon them any tribute or head tax, but they shall be free from the service of the king.

And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your Elokim, which is in your hand and you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your Elokim, which is in your hand [and which is] greater than that of the judges and the magistrates who judge all the people beyond the river to the side of Yisrael, the people knowledgeable in the Torah.
and whoever does not know and the judge who does not know how to judge, inform him of the judgment that he should execute it.
And whoever does not fulfill and whoever does not fulfill the law of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the law of the king promptly, viz. that he delays the law and the judgment.
judgment The judgment shall be inflicted upon him, upon the one who obstructs justice.
whether to be executed [as translated,] whether to be executed.
uprooted whether to uproot him from the world, him, his offspring and his family (לִשְּׁרשִׁי is desraziner in Old French, to uproot).
fined to be punished with money.

or tortured or to torture him with tortures. Until here is the writ of the letter that King Daryavesh gave to Ezra the scribe in order that he convey it to Yerushalayim to show it to the priests and the Leviyim and the king’s treasurers, in order that they persist in performing the commandments and worshiping Hashem in the Temple and keeping the Torah properly.
Blessed be Hashem Ezra wrote this in his Book when he gave thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He.
and his advisers They are his seven advisers mentioned above (verse 14).

according to the hand of Hashem my Elokim upon me as the help of the Holy One, blessed be He, was upon me; and I gathered from Bnei Yisrael remaining in Bavel the chiefs of the fathers’ houses and the great men to ascend with me from Bavel.
And these are the heads of their fathers’ houses of the immigrants.
and the lineage and their lineage to which they attributed their descent.
Artachshasta He is Daryavesh.
Of the sons of Shchanyah, of the sons of Parosh That is one family, and Zecharyah was the head of the family.
and with him With his lineage, the males of his family traced their lineage.
Eved the son of Jonathan That was his name.
the last ones who were the last ones to go after Ezra.
to the flowing river Heb. אֶל הַנָהָר הַבָּא, lit. to the coming river.
to Ahava to that river.
and we encamped there and we were camping there.
and I surveyed the people I directed my attention to survey the people who had gathered with me.
And I sent to Eliezer...the heads the great men.
the wise men Heb. מְבִינִים, lit. understanding. They were wise men.
And I commanded them, etc. I sent them and commanded them to speak to Ido, who was the greatest and most esteemed in Kasifya.
to Ido Heb. עַל אִדוֹ, lit. about Ido.
and I put...into their mouth I put into their mouth words to speak as my emissary to Ido and his brother, who were placed and settled in Kasifya, to bring us servants to serve in the Temple.
in Kasifya the name of a place in Bavel.
Ahiv the name of a man.
who were settled Heb. הַנְתִינִים, like הַנְתוּנִים, those who were settled. Therefore, it is written with a “vav.”
according to the hand of our Elokim just as the success of the Holy One, blessed be He, was upon us.
a man of intellect a wise man.
of the sons of Machli... All these were Leviyim.
And of the Nethinites And of the slaves, the Nethnites that King David had appointed, and the chefs of Yisrael ascended with them.
to fast Heb. לְהִתְעַנוֹת to fast.
a straight way that the Omnipresent lead us in peace.
For I was ashamed For I was ashamed of the king, and I did not wish to request of him chariots and horsemen in order to guide us.
for we had said For we had already said to King Daryavesh that the Holy One, blessed be He, benefits those who seek Him and pours out His wrath and His anger upon those who forsake Him.
and He accepted our prayer for we arrived safely in Yerushalayim.

And I separated And when I was there by the river Ahava, I separated some of the chiefs of the priests and weighed out the silver and the gold for them to deposit into the treasuries of the House of Hashem.
which...had offered which those living in Bavel had offered.
and one hundred silver vessels by talents one talent for each vessel.
And...sprinkling bowls bowls for sprinkling [the blood of the sacrifices].
of one thousand darics a type of coin. There were one thousand darics in these twenty sprinkling bowls of gold.
golden of golden copper (or) a type of copper coin.
fine Heb. טוֹבָה, the feminine form, modifying copper (נְחֹשֶּׁת).
two two vessels.
precious as gold Heb. חֲמוּדוֹת כַּזָהָב. He calls the vessels חֲמוּדוֹת in the feminine form.
to them to these chiefs of the priests.
the chambers of the House of Hashem in order to deposit them in the chambers of the Temple.
on the twelfth of the first month on the twelfth of Nissan
the hand of our Elokim was upon us to cause us to succeed in the way that we traversed.
Everything was counted and weighed The number of the vessels and their weights was the same when they received them as when they itemized them.
Those coming from captivity, the people of the exile those who came with Ezra.
offered up burnt offerings all were burnt offerings, and it was a temporary ruling.
And they gave the king’s decrees These returnees from exile related King Daryavesh’s mandate to the officers of the king, those who see his face.
and the governors Heb. וּפַחֲווֹת, like וְפַחוֹת.
the land beyond the river those on the side of the land of Yisrael, who are considered as being beyond the river of the inhabitants of Bavel.
and they exalted They were exalting and assisting.
these these incidents that related the kings’ decrees.
the chiefs of Yisrael.
saying And so they said to me.
was first in this treachery for they commenced to deal treacherously by intermarrying with the peoples of the lands.
bewildered Heb. מְשּׁוֹמֵם miserable and bewildered, like (Ez. 3:15): “...seven days bewildered among them.”
from my fast for I had not eaten on that day.

we were delivered Heb. נִתַּנוּ, like נִתַּנְנוּ. The “dagesh” in the “nun” is instead of another “nun,” like (II Chron. 14:10): “for we rely (תִשְּׁעַנוּ) on You,” like נִשְּׁעַנְנוּ. (Gen. 34:16): “... then we will give (וְנָתַנוּ) our daughters,” like וְנָתַנְנוּ.
as of this day as appears this day, for the Ten Tribes have already been exiled, and many of the exiles still remain in Bavel.
And now, for a short moment temporarily.
favor Heb. תְּחִנָה, like חֲנִינָה
and to give us a peg to establish us in the land of Yisrael.
a peg יָתֵד, like (Isa. 22:23): “And I will thrust him like a peg (יָתֵד) in a sure place.”
a little life [as translated,] a little life.
For we are slaves to Daryavesh, king of Paras.
has not forsaken us Heb. לֹא עֲזָבָנוּ, a combination of לֹא עָזַב אוֹתָנוּ.
and He has extended Heb. וַיַט, an expression of the causative, like מַטֶה. He extended His loving-kindness upon us.
a fence for they had created a fence to keep His commandments.
unclean Heb. נִדָה, unclean and repulsive.
and you shall cause...to inherit You shall give the land to your children as an inheritance to eternity.
And after all that has come upon us after all the calamity that has befallen us because of our evil deeds.

You have punished less You have held back from our iniquities until below them [i.e., less than them], for our iniquity was lessened by the expiation effected by our exile. We may also interpret it in this manner: You held Yourself back from collecting from us all our iniquity, and You collected from us below [less than] the iniquities, and You requited us according to all our sins.
If we revert Heb. הֲנָשּׁוּב, if we return.
will You not be wroth with us a wonder with an affirmative answer.
for we cannot lit. for there is nothing; i.e., we do not have the power of good deeds to stand and exist before You, because of this transgression.
weeping Heb. בּכֶה, like בֶּכִי.
and we have taken And we took them in.
there is hope There is hope for Yisrael concerning this, for they can cast out their foreign wives and their offspring and cast out all the children born from these foreign wives.
by the counsel of the Lord by the counsel and the will of the Holy One, blessed be He.
and those who hasten to [perform] the commandment of our Elokim and the Elokim-fearers, they shall cast them out.
and according to the Law it shall be done he who performs this act, who will cast out his gentile wife and children.
and we are with you to agree with you.
a proclamation Heb. קוֹל, lit. a voice, an announcement.
by three days at the end of three days.
the ninth month That is the month of Kislev.
quaking over the matter They were afraid over the matter. They were afraid of the stumbling block of this transgression.
and because of the rains And because of the rains that were falling upon them there, they were shivering and miserable.
confess Heb. תּוֹדָה, [which, in this case, means] וִדּוּי, confession.
and it is the rainy season for the rains are falling upon us.
and the work And this separation from sin cannot be executed so quickly.
with the entire congregation Heb. לְכָל הַקָהָל
who took in Heb. הַהשִּׁיב equivalent to אֲשֶּׁר הוֹשִּׁיב.
until we avert until the burning anger of the Holy One, blessed be He, returns from upon us.
stood up against this to argue concerning this matter.
supported them strengthened their hands.
to investigate Heb. לְדַרְיוֹשּׁ, like לִדְרוֹשּׁ.
And they completed everything And they completed the rectification of the matter of the men who had brought in heathen wives, for they cast them out.
of the first month until the first day of Nissan.
And they advised them Heb. וַיִתְּנוּ יָדָם, lit. and they gave their hand, their advice, like (II Sam. 14:19): “Behold Yoav’s advice (יַד יוֹאָב) is with you in all this (sic).”
for their guilt This was a temporary ruling.
And of the sons of Imer All these are priests until (verse 23): “And of the Leviyim, etc.”
and some of them had wives by whom they had children And some of them had heathen wives by whom they had children. They cast out all of them, both the wives and the children.
